scope: New independent GEMV branch only; no imports of torch/Triton during this review, no GPU execution, no checkpoint read, no runtime adapter/table edits.
arithmetic: Existing native unpack helper uses the same asymmetric group128 packed order [0,16,4,20,8,24,12,28].
FP32 subtract/multiply of exactly represented uint4 differences and FP16 scale, then explicit FP16 weight round before FP32 x multiplication; native FP16 scale product has this same rounding target.
Bounded BK128/256 tiles, runtime K loop, FP32 tile reduction and FP32 running accumulation; split1 casts final output to FP16.
Split2/4/8 writes disjoint FP32 partial[split,N], including zero for empty splits, then a separate small FP32 sum and FP16 cast. No atomics, no zero-initialization dependency.
Reduction ordering differs from Tensor Core GEMM and original FP16 split-atomic behavior; mathematical-format agreement is not bitwise output equivalence.

tiny_scalar_math_check.scope: Python arithmetic sanity only; not a Triton numerical or device-memory gate

cpu_checks.bytecode_compilation_without_execution: passed for both new files; no pycache written

register_and_bandwidth_review.caveat: Tile elements/thread is only a pressure indicator, not measured register count. Large BK256/BN128 with 2 warps has 512 logical elements/thread and may spill or fail; failures are retained. GPU receipts record n_regs/n_spills/shared when Triton exposes them.
register_and_bandwidth_review.packed_access: Load [BK,BN/8] packed int32 only once, then reuse native unpack; load only BK/128 zero/scale rows before broadcast across each 128-row group. BN32 packed row is16bytes, BN64 is32bytes, BN128 is64bytes; narrow tiles may lose transaction efficiency.
register_and_bandwidth_review.parallelism: CTA count is ceil(N/BN)*split. Example N2560 gives80/40/20 CTAs before split for BN32/64/128. Split may increase parallelism but adds a second launch and FP32 partial read/write; many-output gate_up already has many CTAs.
register_and_bandwidth_review.x_traffic: Logical x reads before cache reuse add 4/BN of packed-weight bytes:12.5%,6.25%,3.125% for BN32/64/128. x is small and likely reused in cache; this is not measured DRAM traffic.
register_and_bandwidth_review.precision_tradeoff: CUDA-core dequant/multiply/reduction avoids the BM16 Tensor Core replicated M work but sacrifices Tensor Core throughput and adds cross-thread reduction. Neither direction is assumed faster.

selected_validation.tensor_sha: Each real fused qweight/scales/qzeros tensor hashed

tail_tests.configurations: Selected configurations plus BK256/BN32/split8 stress case; all masked K/N/groups and empty split outputs

gpu_probe_protocol.timings: Hot search12 graph replays; independent randomized two-round confirmations with40 hot and20 cold samples per implementation per round. Both GEMV and partial-reduction kernels remain inside timed replay.
gpu_probe_protocol.cold: 96MiB GPU add_ before each begin CUDA event; observed whole-buffer checksum and count; never include eviction time in kernel intervals or silently choose winner from cold results.
gpu_probe_protocol.failure_handling: Append every attempt including numerical/resource/compiler failure; stop on device faults. All-unsuitable branches retain result/attempts and install no runtime table. Nonfinite numerical values are JSON-safe nulls with passed=false.
gpu_probe_protocol.concurrency: Probe takes both existing study/GPU advisory locks before importing torch or reading checkpoint.
gpu_probe_protocol.decision: Predeclared screening threshold: beat both native and saved wide in hot; at least3% cold gain against both. If no projection passes, stop. If only some pass, root may consider a later selective hybrid adapter; no automatic full-model deployment.

still_required: Actual Triton compile/device launch and real numerical validation; AST cannot prove CUDA compatibility.
Independent review of resource/launch failures and cold confirmation; selection from hot alone is not performance proof.
Any later service integration must preserve prefill baseline and prove M1 capture/replay routes, same-weight full-model token equivalence, fair fixed-input latency and navigation gates.
